from_quote: my last address established this position, that to reduce the thirteen States into one government, would prove the destruction of our liberties
rationale: The paragraph refers to Brutus's "last address" and states its position, the subject of Brutus I (October 18, 1787); this essay appeared November 1, 1787.

from_quote: the trial of all crimes, except in cases of impeachment, shall be by jury ; and such trial shall be in the State where the said crimes shall have been committed.
rationale: The paragraph quotes, in quotation marks, the opening words of Article III, Section 2, clause 3 (up to "committed"), omitting the word "held".
to_quote: The Trial of all Crimes, except in Cases of Impeachment, shall be by Jury; and such Trial shall be held in the State where the said Crimes shall have been committed

from_quote: the general government will have the sole power to raise and to pay armies
rationale: The paragraph names the power of the general government "to raise and to pay armies", the power granted in Article I, Section 8, clause 12.

from_quote: the writ of habeas corpus shall not be suspended, unless
rationale: The paragraph names "the ninth section of the first article" and reproduces the words of its habeas corpus clause ("unless in cases of rebellion", shortened from the clause).
to_quote: the Writ of Habeas Corpus shall not be suspended, unless

from_quote: no bill of attainder, or ex post facto law, shall be passed
rationale: The paragraph names "the ninth section of the first article" and reproduces the words of Article I, Section 9, clause 3.
to_quote: No Bill of Attainder or ex post facto Law shall be passed

from_quote: no title of nobility shall be granted by the United States
rationale: The paragraph names "the ninth section of the first article" and reproduces the opening words of Article I, Section 9, clause 8.
to_quote: No Title of Nobility shall be granted by the United States

from_quote: That this Constitution, and the laws of the United States which shall be made in pursuance thereof, and all treaties made, or which shall be made, under the authority of the United States, shall be the supreme law of the land ; and the judges in every State shall be bound thereby, any thing in the Constitution, or laws of any State, to the contrary notwithstanding.
rationale: The paragraph quotes, in quotation marks, the clause it introduces as "expressed in positive and unequivocal terms in the sixth article".
to_quote: This Constitution, and the Laws of the United States which shall be made in Pursuance thereof; and all Treaties made, or which shall be made, under the Authority of the United States, shall be the supreme Law of the Land; and the Judges in every State shall be bound thereby, any Thing in the Constitution or Laws of any State to the Contrary notwithstanding.

from_quote: The senators and representatives before-mentioned, and the members of the several State legislatures, and all executive and judicial officers, both of the United States, and of the several States, shall be bound, by oath or affirmation, to support this Constitution.
rationale: The paragraph, which continues the quotation from the sixth article begun in the previous paragraph, quotes in quotation marks the first part of Article VI, clause 3.
to_quote: The Senators and Representatives before mentioned, and the Members of the several State Legislatures, and all executive and judicial Officers, both of the United States and of the several States, shall be bound by Oath or Affirmation, to support this Constitution

from_quote: The power to make treaties, is vested in the president, by and with the advice and consent of two-thirds of the senate.
rationale: The paragraph names the treaty power of the president "by and with the advice and consent" of the senate, echoing the words of Article II, Section 2, clause 2.
to_quote: by and with the Advice and Consent of the Senate, to make Treaties
